clue.text: Husband comes in to fix desk that's easily mended?

indicators.note: the husband's letter comes in, entering the middle of the joined words for fix and desk

parts.note: to fix a race or result is to rig it
a desk is a kind of table to write on

explanation.surface: Someone hoping a husband will come round to repair a desk that should be simple to sort out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be put right or set straight again is readily repaired.

clue.text: Come back with little money in bank

indicators.note: the small coin letter sits in the middle of the word for bank, the verb

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
P, for penny or pence, is a small amount of British money

explanation.surface: Advice to return from a trip with only a few coins left in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun holding money; it is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer or respond is to come back with words of your own.

clue.text: Information about accommodation given to married members of wedding party

indicators.note: the information word goes about, wrapping round, the lodging and the marital abbreviation

parts.note: GEN is British slang for information
rooms are accommodation at a hotel or lodging

explanation.surface: Details about the hotel rooms passed on to the newlyweds' party.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British English for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ushers and supporters of the bridegroom are part of the bridal entourage.

clue.text: Striker regularly missing fixture

indicators.note: every other letter of the word striker goes missing, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A football striker is regularly absent from the team's match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly missing' drops S, R, K and R, keeping the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A match or fixture in sport, especially a cup draw, is called a tie.

clue.text: Driver having drink needs to belt up

parts.note: Jenson Button is a British Formula One racing driver
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A motorist who has had a drink is told to fasten the seat belt.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenson Button was the 2009 F1 world champion; IT is short for Italian vermouth in the pub order 'gin and It'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang telling someone to stop talking and be quiet.

clue.text: Wild beasts in Ireland, surprisingly

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the words Ireland, surprisingly

explanation.surface: An unexpected report of wild animals roaming in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elands are large African antelopes, wild animals of the savannah.

clue.text: Port we located in Aegean island

indicators.note: the word we is placed inside the name of the Greek island

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea

explanation.surface: A traveller saying the harbour they found was on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: COWES is a harbour town on the Isle of Wight, home of a famous sailing regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town on the Isle of Wight, it is a sailing seaport.

clue.text: Lib-Dem limits money allocated to university repeatedly

indicators.note: the coalition phrase forms the limits, enclosing the money and college letters

parts.note: in the 2010 coalition a Liberal Democrat was a Conservative ally, CON ALLY
TIN is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A complaint that the Liberal Democrats cap the money given to universities over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats governed in coalition with the Conservatives from 2010, so a Lib-Dem was an ally of the Tories, the British right-wing party.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something again and again without stopping is doing it constantly.

clue.text: Labour leader's promise about the environment

indicators.note: the pledge word goes about, around, the leading letter

parts.note: to give your word is to make a promise

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of the Labour Party pledges action on green issues.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet and the setting we all live in make up our surroundings.

clue.text: Every partner delighted to start in position for ballroom routine

indicators.note: the starting letters go in the middle of the word for position

parts.note: a stance is a position or way of standing

indicators.note: the opening letters of each of three words are taken

explanation.surface: Each dancing partner is thrilled to take their place for a ballroom number.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance built on fixed footwork patterns is a set routine of steps.

clue.text: Plan for getting about in aircraft

parts.note: PRO is Latin-derived for, in favour of

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about goes in the middle of the aircraft word

parts.note: a jet is a jet-propelled aircraft
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A scheme for getting around by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: C is short for Latin circa, 'about', used with dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or undertaking that is planned out is a venture or design.

clue.text: Isn't grass cut short on racecourse?

parts.note: AIN'T is a colloquial form of isn't

indicators.note: the word for grass loses its last letter, cut off at the end

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places

explanation.surface: A question whether the lawn isn't being mown short at the track.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE, near Liverpool, is the racecourse of the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is the English course where the Grand National horse race is run.

clue.text: For starters you'd avoid mushy vegetable

indicators.note: the starters of words are their first letters, taken from the next three

explanation.surface: A diner's advice: as a first course, steer clear of the soggy greens.
explanation.definitionFit: A yam is a starchy tropical tuber eaten as a root crop.

clue.text: Liberal has American woman taken care of

parts.note: BROAD is old US slang for a woman
minded means looked after, as a child is minded

explanation.surface: A progressive person has a woman from America looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerant and open to other views is what a liberal attitude means.

clue.text: A basic term I translated for some exotic food?

indicators.note: translated means turned into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A simple word, once translated, names an unusual dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-grained fragrant grain from India and Pakistan is a foreign foodstuff.

clue.text: Make me endure endless violence at home

parts.note: to do is to make or perform

indicators.note: the word for endure loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: to stick something is to endure or put up with it

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being made to suffer unending abuse inside the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endure' is STICK, as in 'I can't stick it'; a DOMESTIC is British slang for a household row.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a noun for a family quarrel or fight in the house.

clue.text: Car component making rides back quite bumpy

indicators.note: a bumpy ride jumbles things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Driving goes rough on the return journey because of a faulty part.
explanation.definitionFit: A braking device clamping a rotating disc stops the wheels of a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Thus make no interest?

parts.note: turning the two letters of the word on round makes the word no, so this instruction builds these clue words

explanation.surface: A question whether this produces no interest at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, turns the letters O and N round to give the clue's last word; 'Thus' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse or excite someone is to stir their interest; the query flags the loose sense.

clue.text: Mention about a mass being led by cardinal in cathedral

indicators.note: the word for mention goes about, around, the colour and the mass letters

parts.note: to note something is to mention it

indicators.note: the mass and its article follow behind, led by the colour

parts.note: cardinal is a bright red colour
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A celebrated Mass said by a cardinal in a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' is the colour, not the churchman the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Gothic church in Paris is the city's famous cathedral.

clue.text: Delay short vacation at seaside town

parts.note: HOL is a shortened form of holiday
Dover is a port town on the English Channel coast

explanation.surface: A brief holiday at the seaside is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is the Kent port by the white cliffs.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold over is to postpone or defer something to later.

clue.text: Holiday souvenir, perhaps, one I brought from Tunisian resort

indicators.note: resort here means sort again, rearranging the letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A tan picked up at a North African beach resort to show off at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Take two Is (one and I) out of TUNISIAN and 'resort' the rest; 'resort' looks like a beach town.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronzed skin brought back from a sunny trip is a keepsake of the break.

clue.text: European taken in by libertine's game

indicators.note: the Latvian goes inside the rake's word

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a libertine
a Lett is a native of Latvia

explanation.surface: A visitor from Europe is conned by a rake's gambling game.
explanation.walkthrough: European is not E here but LETT, an old name for a Latvian.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino gambling game with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Clever fellow's item of angling equipment

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
ROD is a man's name, giving a fellow

explanation.surface: A smart man's fishing tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: A light rod for casting artificial lures is fishing tackle.

clue.text: Airline company worked during state occasion in France

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: the farming word goes during, inside, the word for state

parts.note: to state is to say
tilled means worked the soil

explanation.surface: An airline was busy during a French national celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national holiday on 14 July marks the storming of a Paris prison.

clue.text: Detailed descriptions of glasses

definitions.meaning: short for spectacles, worn to see

explanation.surface: Specifications for a pair of spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal clipping of both specifications and spectacles.

clue.text: I'll make earth move

definitions.note: read as I will: the self, with the shortened will as link

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring
to go is to move

explanation.surface: A boast of being able to shift the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the I in 'I'll'; the 'll make' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the 'I' of psychology.

clue.text: Winning prize? No, the reverse

indicators.note: the two words before are read backwards as a whole

parts.note: a pot is a prize or trophy
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exchange about whether a prize was won, with the answer being the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the lead or ahead is being in front.

clue.text: Retailer going bust finally abandoned place of work

indicators.note: something going bust breaks apart, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of the shopkeeper word is abandoned

explanation.surface: A shop going bankrupt finally walks out of its premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally abandoned' drops the last R of RETAILER; 'going bust' rearranges RETAILE.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or designer's studio is a workshop.

clue.text: Road worker on edges of village green

indicators.note: the road and worker follow on after the edge letters
the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A man mending the roads on the edge of a village green.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush and covered with grass or plants describes a fresh green landscape.

clue.text: Trash, say, in play area

indicators.note: say signals spoken aloud, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to trash something is to wreck it

explanation.surface: Vandals trashing a playground.
explanation.walkthrough: REC is British short for a recreation ground, a public park or playground.
explanation.definitionFit: A rec, recreation ground, is a public field for games.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, repulsed by English woman

indicators.note: the English letter is placed by, next to, the turned word
repulsed means driven back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an island

explanation.surface: A man rejected by an Englishwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, not a male, and 'repulsed' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's given name, so it stands for a female.

clue.text: Woolly hat priced at affordable cost?

indicators.note: woolly means fuzzy or muddled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knitted hat on sale at a bargain price.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely inexpensive, costing almost nothing, is a bargain price.
